scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: HELP!! Part of our network has FALLEN OFF THE MAP
after one of the boxes restarted. The clever people say the two halves were
held together by some kind of INVISIBLE BRIDGE, which sounds made up to me,
and something around it must be wrong. I always said you can't hold a network
together with something invisible!! Could someone look at it so the far areas
are reachable again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
All tested paths are healthy and no fault exists in the current network state. The Kath5 topology uses an OSPF virtual link between r4 (router ID 14.1.4.1) and r8 (router ID 18.1.4.1), traversing area 1 as the transit area, to connect area 2 to the OSPF backbone. Both sides carry the correct virtual-link peer router ID in their running configurations, and both report a Full adjacency on VLINK0 — uptime 7m51s from r4, confirming the link survived and reconverged after whatever restart the ticket describes.

Area 2 on r8 shows zero internal OSPF adjacencies because its only non-virtual-link interfaces are loopback addresses and the single-router stub segment BB — no other router connects there. This is expected topology design, not a fault. The ospf_snapshot orphan/divergence flags for area 2 are architectural noise, not symptoms.

Beyond OSPF, r11 bridges to a separate EIGRP 100 domain (r12, r13) by redistributing EIGRP routes into OSPF area 3 and carrying a kernel default route on r12 that allows the return path. pc12's subnet (120.0.0.0/8) reaches the backbone correctly via this redistribution. End-to-end reachability between pc0 and pc12 is 0% loss in both directions, and area 2 networks (80.1.1.1, 18.1.1.1) are fully reachable from pc0. infra_sweep, l2_snapshot, and pressure_sweep are all clean across all 15 devices.

Root cause: no current fault — the OSPF virtual link and full routing fabric are operating correctly. The reported outage was a transient convergence delay following a device restart, now fully resolved.

Fix: no corrective action required; monitor for recurrence of the triggering restart.
